newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsicans fire on buildings after remands.
newsitem.headline: Corsicans fire on buildings after remands.

text.p: Suspected separatists shot up three government buildings overnight in Corsica after the island's best-known separatist leader was remanded in custody in Paris, police said on Wednesday.

No one was hurt in the shootings against the prefecture (central government) building in the north Corsica town of Bastia and against gendarmerie offices or barracks at Bastia airport and the small mountain town of Belgodere, police said.
Several gendarmes were present when bullets fired from the outside smashed into the walls of a room at the airport.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the attacks which followed the surrender to police in Bastia on Monday of Francois Santoni, general secretary of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal facade of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing.
Santoni and his girlfriend, a lawyer for the movement, were remanded in custody in Paris late on Tuesday and probed for attempted extortion and bomb attacks by France's top anti-terrorist judge.

Magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere formally placed Santoni and Marie-Helene Mattei under investigation on suspicion of belonging to a group involved in terrorist activities, recreating a banned organisation, extortion and complicity in destruction of property by explosives.
The government ordered a crackdown after separatists stepped up attacks in a two-decade-old campaign to demand greater autonomy from Paris for the Mediterranean holiday island.
Santoni surrendered to police after Mattei was detained in connection with a bomb attack on a Corsican golf club linked to an attempt to extort protection money known as a "revolutionary tax".

The club's owner refused to pay four million francs ($800,000) and, in a rare act of cooperation with the police in Corsica, called in detectives after the groundsman's house was blown up last Thursday.
Santoni had been on the run since he was sentenced in his absence in October to four months in prison for carrying guns.
The FLNC has claimed a string of recent bomb attacks in Corsica and on the French mainland, including one on the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux.

The separatists have threatened "new forms" of attacks in Corsica and on the mainland. French radio said the government, fearing retaliation for the detention of Santoni, was beefing up security forces on the island with 100 riot police.
